a.headline: Sekondo Puts ChatGPT and Claude Inside After Effects and Premiere Pro
a.summary: A new plugin called Sekondo embeds large language models directly into six Adobe applications, letting motion designers prompt AI without leaving their editing environment. This is worth watching as a case study in how AI assistance is being woven into the core tools of motion design production.

a.headline: In the Age of AI, Curiosity Is Our Greatest Creative Tool
a.summary: This piece from the DTTO 2026 branding conference argues that curiosity and genuine creative inquiry remain the irreplaceable differentiators for designers working alongside AI tools. It is a useful provocation for students navigating how to maintain a distinct creative voice in an increasingly automated industry.

b.headline: National Grid to site biggest substation in UK near planned Teesside datacentre
b.summary: The UK is building its largest ever electricity substation specifically to support a major incoming AI data centre on Teesside, revealing the enormous grid-level infrastructure demands of scaling AI. This is a concrete example of how the hunger for AI compute is reshaping national energy planning in ways that have direct carbon and resource implications.

b.headline: The agentic web is here
b.summary: MIT Technology Review examines the rise of autonomous AI agents that browse, transact, and act on the web on behalf of users, a shift that dramatically multiplies the compute and energy cycles AI systems consume at scale. As these agents proliferate, the cumulative environmental footprint of even routine digital tasks is set to grow significantly.

c.headline: AI is stealing Indigenous Australian art and churning out Temu slop, artist says
c.summary: The chair of the National Gallery of Australia First Nations advisory group has spoken out against AI systems scraping and replicating Indigenous Australian art, describing the output as devaluing both the cultural authenticity and the livelihoods of living artists. This is essential reading for understanding how AI image generation causes direct harm to specific creative communities whose work has particular cultural and spiritual significance.

c.headline: Disquiet grows in Albanese back yard as Grayndler artists unite against insane AI proposal
c.summary: Artists and designers in inner-west Sydney are organising against proposed changes to Australian copyright law that would allow AI companies to train models on creative work without consent or compensation. The campaign is a live example of creative communities mobilising politically against the legal frameworks that enable AI appropriation of their labour.

c.headline: Google search has gone from being very handy to useless
c.summary: Guardian cartoonist First Dog on the Moon uses comic illustration to skewer the way AI summaries have degraded Google Search into a tool that actively undermines the open web it was built on. The piece is a sharp example of how satirical visual communication can critique AI product decisions more pointedly than conventional journalism.

c.headline: Wildwood: a big leap forward for animation that you need to see on a big screen
c.summary: Laika Studios has released Wildwood, a feature film built entirely on handmade stop-motion craft combined with CG, representing a major creative and commercial bet on physical, labour-intensive animation at a moment when studios are rushing toward AI-generated imagery. The piece makes a passionate case for why tactile, human-made animation carries an emotional register that synthetic tools cannot replicate.

c.headline: This celebrity ad shows what a difference it makes when you dont use CGI
c.summary: A new financial services campaign shot entirely with practical effects has been praised for its warmth and tactility precisely because audiences are now so saturated with synthetic digital imagery that real physical filmmaking reads as surprising and refreshing. For motion design students, this is a timely reminder that restraint and materiality can be the most powerful creative choice in a CGI-saturated visual landscape.

c.headline: Design Week student challenge: bringing human creativity back to summer fetes
c.summary: Following a surge in AI-generated community event posters, Design Week challenged graphic design students to create hand-crafted alternatives, raising important questions about default reliance on generative tools. The results show what intentional human authorship looks like when set directly against algorithmic output.
